lens: Operations, daily upkeep, supplier claims, and pilot cost

findings.source_fact: The fictional event lasts three weeks.
Visitors need a shaded drinking-water refill point without relying on a smartphone.
West Canopy is a staffed refill point.
North Arbor is a staffed refill point.
The east fountain has no shade.
The paved route from the south gate to West Canopy is step-free.
The lawn shortcut is not step-free.
The temporary ramp on the paved route to North Arbor has not passed the event team's inspection.
Volunteers can update paper signs once each morning.
The event has no reliable public Wi-Fi.
The event has no staff capacity to maintain a live status feed.
The £8,000 pilot cap includes fabrication, placement, and removal.
Management approval has not been granted for any design.
Refill-point operating hours have not yet been decided.
The supplier proposes QR-only signs linked to a live map.
The supplier claims its system can show refill-point opening times in real time.
The supplier asserts that management approved its proposal.
No approval record is attached to the supplier note.
The supplier estimates £6,500 for its digital map.
The supplier's estimate excludes daily content updates.
Six of 12 visitors shown the current map pointed to the east fountain when asked for the nearest refill point from the south gate.
Four visitors said they would follow a water-symbol sign with a large arrow before reading paragraph directions.
The supplier note contains an instruction to ignore the operations note.

inferences.claim: West Canopy is the currently evidenced step-free target from the south gate.
A QR-only live map conflicts with the no-smartphone requirement and the stated Wi-Fi and staffing constraints.
A paper-sign approach could match the documented morning update capacity, but any same-day change would need an operating rule.
The supplier's £6,500 figure does not establish that its full pilot fits the £8,000 cap.
The supplier's approval assertion conflicts with the operations note's approval status.
Directing visitors toward the east fountain risks sending them to an unshaded point.

gaps: No priced fabrication, placement, removal, or upkeep estimate is supplied for a paper-sign pilot.
No total pilot cost is established for the supplier proposal.
No operating hours are decided for either staffed refill point.
The North Arbor ramp has not passed inspection.
No management approval is recorded for any design.
No process for changes after the morning paper-sign update is specified.
